text: Archival discussion of possible mechanisms for precognition. It places a causality-reversing tachyon beside advanced-potential solutions as speculative physical possibilities. This is a hypothesis list, not a tachyon detection or validated retrocausal mechanism.
title: Precognition mechanism discussion (archival working label)

text: Final-report material discusses EPR, traversable wormholes and tachyons while treating reverse information flow and precognition as a heuristic model. It considers a possible statistical reversal or breach of causality, with caution about extrapolating microscopic quantum ideas to macroscopic cognition.
title: Phenomenological Research and Analysis: Final Report

text: Decision Augmentation Theory is presented as a phenomenological statistical model. The report says quantum models of the human brain are premature speculation and proposes anomalous transtemporal acquisition or transfer of information from future to past as an informational explanation to be tested against force-like models.
title: Decision Augmentation Theory: Toward a Model of Anomalous Mental Phenomena

text: Research-plan notes define precognition operationally as data received before the source emits it in ordinary space. They discuss information leakage from the future, wormholes or time travel, vector and scalar potentials, and stochastic causality. The same plan notes that relevant vector or scalar propagation experiments had not confirmed the proposed effect to date.
title: Notes: Research Plan

text: Conference summary of Gerald Feinberg's precognition proposal. It notes that electromagnetic theory permits time-retarded and time-advanced solutions, with advanced solutions carrying information from future to past, but also states that these solutions are customarily excluded because they had not been experimentally observed. An attached critique calls the idea trivial.
title: Quantum Physics and Parapsychology — Precognition: A History of Things Future

text: Parapsychological and philosophical discussion of backward causation and retroactive PK. It describes experiments using time-displaced or prerecorded random-number-generator sequences and discusses feedback as a possible route for an apparent effect preceding its cause. The claims are historical experimental assertions, not established physics.
title: Backward Causation / The Relentless Question

text: A multi-year research plan for anomalous mental phenomena. It discusses possible information backwards in time, time reversal at microscopic scales, the macroscopic arrow of time and stochastic causality as research questions. It repeatedly calls for milestone checks, expert oversight, validation attempts and abandonment of tasks if results do not warrant continuation.
title: A Comprehensive Research Plan for Anomalous Mental Phenomena

text: Evaluative report uses precognition for purported information whose source lies in the future and retroactive PK for a purported effect that precedes the cause. Its value here is taxonomy and historical research context rather than confirmation of either phenomenon.
title: An Evaluative Report on the Current Status of Parapsychology

text: Exploratory discussion of advanced-potential or advanced-time solutions in electromagnetic context and of anomalous cognition as an information-channel or access problem. It recommends time-locked analysis of observations before and after a defined time zero rather than treating timing loosely.
title: Advanced-potential / timing analysis discussion (archival working label)

text: June 1995 annotated bibliography that records the lineage of Decision Augmentation Theory papers. It characterizes DAT as a statistical treatment in which anomalous perturbation results may be reinterpreted as anomalous cognition or statistical opportunism, making it useful for source-lineage mapping rather than independent evidence.
title: Annotated Bibliography

text: CIA-held copy of an ordinary theoretical-physics article about tachyons. It discusses tachyon kinematics and frame-dependent time ordering for hypothetical faster-than-light particles. It belongs in the theoretical physics context lane and is not evidence for anomalous cognition or for experimental tachyon detection.
title: Tachyon theoretical-physics article (CIA-held copy)

text: Methodological critique of parapsychology emphasizing unreliable anecdotes, control weaknesses, selective interpretation, replication problems and risks to falsifiability when retroactive or quantum explanations can be invoked after the fact. It is preserved as a disconfirming and methodological control lane.
title: Parapsychology: Science of the Anomalous? — critique lane

text: Final report on electronic-system perturbation includes experimental lineage for random-number-generator and psychokinesis studies, including comparisons involving time displacement and prerecorded versus present-time conditions. Archived experimental lineage is recorded without treating the reported effects as validated.
title: Electronic System Perturbation — Final Report
